nodes.title: Egorov's theorem on the real line under integrable domination

nodes.summary: Let `μ` be a finite measure on `ℝ` (the zero measure included) and `0 < Γ₁ < Γ₂`. Then `∫ E, Γ₁ ^ 2 / (E ^ 2 + Γ₁ ^ 2) ∂μ < ∫ E, Γ₂ ^ 2 / (E ^ 2 + Γ₂ ^ 2) ∂μ` if and only if `μ` gives positive mass to `{0}ᶜ`. The kernel equals `1` at `E = 0` for every width, so mass at the origin never contributes to the increase; in particular the zero measure, and any multiple of the Dirac mass at `0`, give equal integrals.
nodes.title: Strict width monotonicity of Lorentzian integrals

nodes.summary: Let `μ` be a finite measure on `ℝ`; it is nonnegative by type and may be the zero measure. If `0 < Γ₁ ≤ Γ₂`, then `∫ E, Γ₁ ^ 2 / (E ^ 2 + Γ₁ ^ 2) ∂μ ≤ ∫ E, Γ₂ ^ 2 / (E ^ 2 + Γ₂ ^ 2) ∂μ`. Both widths are integrated against the same measure, and equal widths are allowed.
nodes.title: Lorentzian integrals are nondecreasing in the width
